Answer: A
Reason: The combination of spontaneous chest pain, neck swelling (subcutaneous emphysema), and pneumomediastinum immediately following an alcoholic binge (suggesting forceful vomiting/retching) is the classic presentation of Boerhaave syndrome, or esophageal perforation. While alveolar rupture can cause pneumomediastinum, the specific history of alcohol-induced retching strongly points to an esophageal etiology.
